rationale: The L0 layer is defined as a broad functional family for organization and synthesis, not a unitary latent variable.
Valuation and Emotion are distinct but strongly interacting and can be represented cleanly as separate L1 modules inside one composite family.
Reinforcement learning/value updating and Habit are distinct, and model-free RL is not synonymous with habit; they therefore require separate L1 subsystems inside one composite family.
Splitting L0 now would add top-level count without improving reasoning if 10X inference is performed at L1/L2 and core rollups remain descriptive summaries.
A future split remains mandatory if R2/R3 reveals that shared L0 ownership causes retrieval ambiguity, invalid rollups, or benchmark reasoning failures.
runtime_constraint: No 10X conclusion may infer a unitary psychological state from an L0 aggregate alone. L1/L2 mechanisms and measurement provenance must drive reasoning.
replan_triggers: L1/L2 reasoning repeatedly requires mutually incompatible semantics under one core.
Measurement objects cannot be assigned without core-level ambiguity.
Cross-core edges require contradictory directions solely because of composite ownership.
Benchmarks show that core aggregation loses causally relevant distinctions.
